translation_en: Yahya also narrated it, that Abu Salamah told him that Abu Hurayrah told him he heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Abu Nu‘aym narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Allah has protective jealousy, and Allah’s protective jealousy is that a believer should do what Allah has forbidden.’

Mahmud narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Al-Zubayr married me when he owned no property, slave, or anything else on earth besides a water-carrying camel and his horse. I used to feed his horse, draw water, mend its water bag, and knead dough, but I did not know how to bake bread. Some honest women from the Ansar, my neighbors, used to bake for me. I would carry date stones on my head from the land the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had granted to al-Zubayr. It was two-thirds of a farsakh from me. One day, I was carrying the date stones on my head when I met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with a group of Ansar. He called me and said, ‘Ikh, ikh,’ inviting me to ride behind him. I felt shy about traveling with the men and remembered al-Zubayr and his jealousy; he was the most jealous of people. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, realized that I was shy, so he went on. I came to al-Zubayr and said, ‘I met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while I was carrying date stones on my head. He was with a group of his Companions. He made his camel kneel for me to ride, but I felt shy before him and remembered your jealousy.’ He said, ‘By Allah, your carrying the date stones was harder on me than your riding with him.’ She said: After that, Abu Bakr sent me a servant who took care of the horse for me, and it was as though he had freed me.

‘Ali narrated to us: Ibn ‘Ulayyah narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was at the house of one of his wives when one of the Mothers of the Believers sent a platter containing food. The wife in whose house the Prophet was struck the servant’s hand, and the platter fell and broke. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gathered the pieces of the platter, then began gathering the food that had been on it into the pieces, saying, ‘Your mother has become jealous.’ He kept the servant there until a platter was brought from the house of the wife where he was. He gave the intact platter to the wife whose platter had been broken and kept the broken one in the house of the wife who had broken it.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘I entered—or came to—Paradise and saw a palace. I asked, “Whose is this?” They said, “It belongs to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.” I wanted to enter it, but I remembered your jealousy and did not.’ ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said, ‘Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Prophet of Allah! Would I be jealous of you?’

‘Abdan narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ibn al-Musayyib informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he said, ‘While I was asleep, I saw myself in Paradise. There was a woman performing ablution beside a palace. I asked, “Whose is this?” They said, “It belongs to ‘Umar.” I remembered his jealousy, so I turned away and left.’ ‘Umar wept while he was in the gathering, then said, ‘Would I be jealous of you, Messenger of Allah?’

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to me, ‘I know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry with me.’ I asked, ‘How do you know that?’ He said, ‘When you are pleased with me, you say, “No, by the Lord of Muhammad.” When you are angry, you say, “No, by the Lord of Ibrahim.”’ She said: I replied, ‘Yes, by Allah, Messenger of Allah; I only leave out your name.’

Ahmad ibn Abi Raja’ narrated to me: Al-Nadr narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah, who said: I was never as jealous of any wife of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, as I was of Khadijah, because the Messenger of Allah mentioned her so often and praised her. Revelation had come to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, instructing him to give her glad tidings of a house for her in Paradise made of hollowed pearl.

Qutaybah narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say from the pulpit, ‘The Banu Hisham ibn al-Mughirah have asked my permission to marry their daughter to ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib. I will not give permission; I will not give permission; I will not give permission, unless ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib wants to divorce my daughter and marry their daughter. She is a part of me; what troubles her troubles me, and what harms her harms me.’ This is the wording he used.

Hafs ibn ‘Umar al-Hawdi narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I will surely tell you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, which no one other than me will tell you. I heard the Messenger of Allah say, ‘Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will become widespread, adultery will become widespread, wine drinking will become widespread, men will become few and women will become many, until one man will be responsible for 50 women.’

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Beware of entering upon women.’ A man from the Ansar said, ‘Messenger of Allah, what about the husband’s male relatives?’ He said, ‘The husband’s male relatives are death.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: ‘Amr narrated to us, from Abu Ma‘bad, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘No man should be alone with a woman unless a close male relative of hers is with them.’ A man stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, my wife has gone out for Hajj, and I have been enlisted for such-and-such expedition.’ He said, ‘Go back and perform Hajj with your wife.’

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: A woman from the Ansar came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he was alone with her. He said, ‘By Allah, you are among the people most beloved to me.’

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was with her while a mukhannath was in the house. The mukhannath said to ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umm Salamah’s brother, ‘If Allah grants you victory over al-Ta’if tomorrow, I will show you the daughter of Ghaylan: when she comes toward you, she has four folds, and when she turns away, she has eight.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Let this man never enter upon you.’

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from al-Awza‘i, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, screen me with his cloak while I watched the Abyssinians playing in the mosque, until I was the one who grew tired. So consider what allowance should be made for a young girl eager for entertainment.

Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra’ narrated to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said: Sawdah bint Zam‘ah went out at night. ‘Umar saw her, recognized her, and said, ‘By Allah, Sawdah, you are not hidden from us.’ She returned to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and told him about it. He was in my room eating dinner, with a piece of meat in his hand. Revelation came to him and then lifted. He said, ‘You women have been given permission to go out for your needs.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘When one of you is asked by his wife for permission to go to the mosque, he should not prevent her.’

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: My uncle by breastfeeding came and asked permission to enter, but I refused to let him in until I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The Messenger of Allah came, and I asked him about it. He said, ‘He is your uncle, so let him in.’ I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, a woman breastfed me; a man did not.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘He is your uncle, so let him enter upon you.’ ‘A’ishah said: This was after the command of hijab had been given to us. ‘A’ishah said: What is forbidden through breastfeeding is the same as what is forbidden through birth.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘A woman should not describe another woman to her husband as though he were looking at her.’

‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A‘mash narrated to us, saying: Shaqiq narrated to me, saying: I heard ‘Abd Allah say: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘A woman should not describe another woman to her husband as though he were looking at her.’

Mahmud narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, said, ‘Tonight I will go around to 100 women, and each will give birth to a boy who will fight in the way of Allah.’ The angel said to him, ‘Say, “If Allah wills.”’ But he did not say it and forgot. He went to them all, but none of them gave birth except one woman, who gave birth to half a person. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Had he said, “If Allah wills,” he would not have broken his oath, and that would have been more likely to fulfill his wish.’

Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Muharib ibn Dithar narrated to us, saying: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, disliked a man coming to his family unexpectedly at night.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: ‘Asim ibn Sulayman informed us, from al-Sha‘bi, who heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘If one of you has been away for a long time, he should not come to his family at night without warning.’

Musaddad narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Sayyar, from al-Sha‘bi, from Jabir, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on an expedition. When we returned, I hurried ahead on a slow camel. A rider caught up with me from behind. I turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He said, ‘Why are you hurrying?’ I said, ‘I have recently married.’ He asked, ‘Did you marry a virgin or a previously married woman?’ I replied, ‘A previously married woman.’ He said, ‘Why not a young woman with whom you could play and who could play with you?’ When we arrived and were about to enter, he said, ‘Wait until you enter at night—that is, in the evening—so that the woman with disheveled hair may comb it and the woman whose husband has been away may groom herself.’ The trustworthy narrator told me that he also said in this hadith, ‘Be eager to have children, Jabir’—meaning, offspring.

Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Sayyar, from al-Sha‘bi, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘When you arrive at night, do not enter upon your family until the woman whose husband has been away has groomed herself and the woman with disheveled hair has combed it.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Be eager to have children.’ ‘Ubayd Allah also related it, from Wahb, from Jabir, from the Prophet, concerning being eager to have children.

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us: Sayyar informed us, from al-Sha‘bi, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on an expedition. When we returned and were near Madinah, I hurried ahead on a slow camel. A rider caught up with me from behind and prodded my camel with a short spear he had with him. My camel then moved as well as the finest camel you could see. I turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have recently married.’ He asked, ‘Have you married?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘A virgin or a previously married woman?’ I replied, ‘A previously married woman.’ He said, ‘Why not a virgin, with whom you could play and who could play with you?’ When we arrived and were about to enter, he said, ‘Wait until you enter at night—that is, in the evening—so that the woman with disheveled hair may comb it and the woman whose husband has been away may groom herself.’

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: People disagreed about what had been used to treat the wound of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on the day of Uhud. They asked Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, who was among the last of the Prophet’s Companions remaining in Madinah. He said, ‘No one still alive knows more about it than I do. Fatimah, peace be upon her, washed the blood from his face, while ‘Ali brought water on his shield. A reed mat was taken, burned, and its ashes were packed into his wound.’

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Sufyan informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, being asked by a man, ‘Did you attend with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr prayer?’ He said, ‘Yes. Were it not for my standing with him, I would not have attended, because I was young.’ He said: The Messenger of Allah went out, prayed, and then gave a sermon. He did not mention a call to prayer or an announcement that the prayer was beginning. Then he went to the women, admonished and reminded them, and commanded them to give charity. I saw them reaching for their ears and necks to hand their jewelry to Bilal. Then he and Bilal went back to his house.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said: Abu Bakr scolded me and began poking me in my side with his hand. Nothing prevented me from moving except that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was there, with his head on my thigh.

Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah about it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Tell him to take her back and keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure again. After that, if he wishes, he may keep her; if he wishes, he may divorce her before touching her. That is the waiting period for which Allah commanded women to be divorced.’

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Sirin, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Umar say: Ibn ‘Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating. ‘Umar mentioned it to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘He should take her back.’ I asked, ‘Is that divorce counted?’ He said, ‘Then what?’ A report from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Umar, also says, ‘Tell him to take her back.’ I asked, ‘Is it counted?’ He replied, ‘What do you think? If he was incapable and foolish?’
